content: Child UX/accessibility (NNG, A11y Collective, Smashing, dyslexia research): target narrow age bands - 9-12 are 'older children' who scan pages (design for scanning, big touch targets, no baby-ish styling); font sizes 12pt baseline for older kids, 14pt younger; WCAG: scalable text to 200% with relative units, 4.5:1 contrast, no justified text, sans-serif fonts with distinguishable letterforms (Open Sans/Verdana) help dyslexia, A-/A+ text-size controls; avoid overstimulating visuals/sounds (ADHD/autism sensory-friendly); want: prominent back button, persistent visible navigation, feedback on every tap. Children 10-12 have roughly adult fine-motor skills but smaller hands - minimum touch target ~44-48 CSS px.
